_meta: An A/B experiment's primary metric plus several guardrail (counter) metrics, used to show why a ship decision must check the guardrails, not just the primary: an intervention that improves the metric you optimized can quietly degrade a metric you also care about (latency, error rate, revenue), and deciding on the primary alone ships that harm. A team optimizes a primary metric -- say engagement -- and the A/B test shows it improved, which feels like a clear win. But an intervention rarely moves only its target: making a feature stickier might slow the page (latency up), surface more errors (error rate up), or cannibalize purchases (revenue down). Guardrail metrics are the secondary metrics you monitor precisely to catch these side effects; each has a direction (higher-is-better or lower-is-better) and a regression limit -- the worst move in the bad direction you are willing to tolerate. A guardrail is breached when it moves in its bad direction by more than its limit. Shipping on the primary alone ignores the guardrails, so a primary win that breaches a guardrail is shipped as a success; a guardrail-aware decision ships only when the primary improves AND no guardrail is breached. metrics lists each metric with its name, its delta in the experiment, whether higher is better, its regression limit (a magnitude in the bad direction), and whether it is the primary. These are the fixture; each guardrail's breach status, and the ship decision under a primary-only rule vs a guardrail-aware rule, are computed.
